### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-notice-guard.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-notice-guard.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1c0ec675ac1c5971c582625cbec010e03bfb32ca` — the merge of head `87411da83042879ee3c0d8a72a22a73ac3f99fe0` into base `ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1c0ec675ac1c5971c582625cbec010e03bfb32ca && git checkout 1c0ec675ac1c5971c582625cbec010e03bfb32ca
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922 87411da83042879ee3c0d8a72a22a73ac3f99fe0 && git checkout -B drift-repro ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922 && git merge --no-ff 87411da83042879ee3c0d8a72a22a73ac3f99fe0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ff88105061012c8b14f7ec937d7b3113e404e922` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `87411da83042879ee3c0d8a72a22a73ac3f99fe0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/save-notice-placement.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-guards.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-notice-guard.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-guard-region-calls.test.ts, .changeset/28846-region-nested-subflow-calls.md + packages/spec/src/automation/control-flow.zod.ts (`collectFlowGraphs`, `MAX_REGION_DEPTH`), packages/spec/src/automation/region-slots.ts (`FLOW_REGION_SLOTS`), packages/services/service-automation/src/region-suspension-refusal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/save-notice-node.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-guard-every-door.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-notice-arming.test.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts (`flow-node-*-flow-alias`), packages/lint/src/flow-cel-root-scope.ts, docs/adr/0126-packaged-metadata-customization-model.md §7.3, hotcrm `src/marketing/flows/campaign-enrollment.flow.ts` and `campaign-member-enroll.flow.ts` (hotcrm checkout `a5982564`)

Review face: the brief asks the narrowing face; `record-recognisers --template --paths` over the PR's file list reads the schema face off the two `packages/spec/src/automation/*` paths (its `hits`). Both map to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and both `hits` are inside `Scope:` above. The three prose paths (`flow.zod.ts`, `save-notice-placement.ts`, `subflow-notice-guard.ts`) are confirmed comment-only in the net diff against `main` (merge-base `b15b634c`, `origin/main` `ff88105061`; `main` has not moved on any touched path since the merge-base): every hunk sits inside a `/** … */` header or a `//` line comment, no token outside a comment changes, and none is a `.describe()` or the TSDoc of an export.

Inputs read: card #28846 body and all four comments (triage 6566019553, claim 6568384018, seat ruling 6568462471, os-dev-report 6569441106); PR #28959 body, file list (7 files, +296/−15) and the net diff `origin/main...87411da8`; the check-runs on `87411da8`. The cited code was read in the tree at `87411da8`; nothing was built, run or re-run.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-02T05:05Z: 20 success, 11 skipped, 30 in progress. Success: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `PR-body guards`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `filter`, `Auto Label`-adjacent jobs. Still in progress at that reading: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, and the `ui/` legs (`Type Check UI`, `Test UI (1–16/16)`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`). None failed. Re-read 2026-11-02T05:21Z after every run completed: 53 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress — `Build Core`, `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI (1–16/16)`, `Build & E2E UI` and `Live E2E UI` all `success`. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts for every derived gate family; nothing was re-run here.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and surface changes the diff implies, each judged against the code as it stands on the head:

1. **`subflowTargets` reads every region depth** (`subflow-guards.ts:62-72`): the top-level graph plus every `loop.body`, every `parallel.branches[i]` and both `try_catch.try` / `try_catch.catch` slots, at every depth up to `MAX_REGION_DEPTH` (32), through `collectFlowGraphs`. Those four slots are exactly `FLOW_REGION_SLOTS` (`region-slots.ts`), the one declaration the parse, the lint walk and the conversion walk all read — so the guards cannot drift from what the spec calls a region. **Right.** The engine's `subflowTargets` docblock already named it "the ONE reading of 'flow A calls flow B' that both directions of the subflow guard share"; a region-nested `subflow` / `map` reaches its child through the same `engine.execute` on every pass, so the top-level-only reading was an implementation gap under that contract, not a reading the contract declared.
2. **Arming decline** (`declineOntoDisabledSubflows` → `disabledPackagedSubflows` → `subflowTargets`): a packaged caller whose region body calls a ledger- or status-disabled packaged child registers, is not armed, warns once, and `/_status` reports `bound: false`, `unboundCause: 'disabled_subflow'` naming the child. Packaged callers only, as before (`engine.ts:5493-5497`). **Right** — pinned by 6 `it.each` cases plus the two-deep `loop { parallel { subflow } }` case.
3. **Re-judge** (`rejudgeSubflowCallers` → `packagedSubflowCallers` and `transitiveSubflowCallers`, both over `subflowTargets`): a child republished `obsolete` disarms a region caller; republished `active` re-arms it. The second loop now re-asks a superset of callers; its `settled` test (`subflowNoticeTrap(...) === undefined` for a bound caller) keeps a caller the notice reading never moved from being flipped. **Right** — pinned (`arming: a child republished obsolete under an armed caller that calls it from a loop body…`).
4. **Switch-off and removal refusal** (`refuseUnderReachingCallers`, via `packagedSubflowCallers`): `toggleFlow(child, false)` and `unregisterFlow(child)` under an enabled packaged caller with a region-nested call are refused with `code: 'DELETE_RESTRICTED'`, `status: 409`, `subflowCallers: [caller]`, the §7.3 sentence; nothing moves. **Right** — pinned (parallel/`map` switch-off, try_catch/`subflow` removal), both halves of the pin present (envelope + `getFlow` still defined).
5. **Enable refusal and ledger-cycle exemption** (`refuseEnableOntoDisabledSubflow` → `disabledPackagedSubflows`; `ledgerDisabledChainReaches` → `subflowTargets`): read the same set by construction (one function). **Right** mechanically; not pinned with a region-nested call in this PR (should-fix 1 below).
6. **The save-notice half of the arming gate stays top-level** (`subflow-notice-guard.ts`: `topLevel()` and `suspendingNode()` unchanged; only the header prose moves). **Right.** `region-suspension-refusal.ts` (#18881, ruling D on #15646) is the standing decision that a region body "runs SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the enclosing run. It cannot park that run on a durable pause", and the refusal is branded un-routable so no container can swallow it. So a region-nested call whose child suspends fails the caller's run at the region boundary; it never suspends the caller and never reaches a `save_notice` after the container. Counting it would decline with `notice_after_suspending_subflow`, a cause that is false for this shape. Pinned by two tests (a notice after a region call; a child whose only suspending call sits in a region). The seat's ruling 6568462471 and the dev's measurement (6/6 cases `failed` at the region boundary, child run left suspended) agree with the code; the stranded child run is #28897, not this PR.
7. **Published surface**: no export added, removed or renamed; `subflow-guards.ts` and `subflow-notice-guard.ts` are not re-exported from the package index; `AutomationEngine.subflowTargets` is `private`. The only consumer-visible change is behavioural (items 2–5). **Right** — `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the correct arm.
8. **`packages/spec`**: no schema, no authorable key, no `.describe()`, no runtime logic (Prime Directive #2 holds); the parse, the save door and `objectstack validate` accept exactly the flows they accepted before. **Right** — `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct, and no spec generated artifact can move (the `Type Check` job's `check:docs` / `check:api-surface` lanes would red it if one did; `Type Check · source gates` is green on the head).
9. **Robustness of the rewrite**: the old body returned `[]` on a non-array `nodes`; the new body hands the flow to `collectFlowGraphs`, which takes `flow.nodes ?? []` and skips non-record members, but would throw on a non-array `nodes`. Every caller reads the flow from `this.flows`, which "only ever holds `FlowSchema.parse` output" (`engine.ts:9589`, set at `:4526`), so `nodes` is always an array there. **Right**; no tolerant fallback was added at the consumer (Prime Directive #12).
10. **Depth ceiling**: a call nested deeper than `MAX_REGION_DEPTH` is unread — the same boundary every spec walk and the parse itself stop at, acknowledged in the PR's acceptance notes. **Right**; not a hole this PR could close on its own.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28846-region-nested-subflow-calls.md`: `'@objectstack/service-automation': patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a `**BREAKING**` banner with Before / Now / Not changed / The fix / Who moves, and exactly one `adr-0087:` marker: `not-required (no-migration-prescription) …`. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines, line-initial, and the title carries `!`.
- Level: the kind is `none`, so the level is `patch` per the Post-Task Checklist ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"). **Matches what the diff publishes**: only `@objectstack/service-automation` ships a behavioural change.
- Disposition: no metadata key is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped; the "fix" in the body is an administrator's enable / republish, not a consumer code rewrite, so `no-migration-prescription` is the honest category and nothing to register in the ADR-0087 registries. `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head.
- No `@objectstack/spec` changeset: the spec diff is comment-only and publishes nothing (no `dist` byte can move from a comment inside a function body or a file-level header that is not an export's TSDoc). This is not a `skip-changeset` label on a publishing diff; it is a non-publishing part of a mixed diff whose publishing part carries its changeset. **Accepted.**
- `Clause-②:` line: `no (narrowing)` — the correct arm; a flow that arms today may decline, and a child switch-off / removal that is accepted today may be refused. Nothing widens.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1 — half (b) of the order (the container rule for the #28840 gate) not implemented: the measured premise was false and the seat withdrew it in ruling 6568462471, filing the region-boundary failure as #28897. Read against `region-suspension-refusal.ts`, the withdrawal is right (① item 6). **Answered.**
- Dev deviation 2 — `subflow-notice-guard.ts` header prose edited: read; the new sentences ("a call inside a region body cannot suspend the run … the run fails at its boundary instead"; "the re-judge … re-asks a superset") are true of the code on the head. **Answered.**
- Dev deviation 3 — no `@objectstack/spec` changeset: **answered** in ②.
- Triage should-fix 1 (spec prose): `save-notice-placement.ts` header and the `flow.zod.ts` wiring comment now say the subflow/map case is met by the arming gate (`notice_after_suspending_subflow`) and that the run-time refusal by name is the residue for a plugin-registered pausing type. Checked against the code: the gate is `engine.ts` `activateFlowTrigger` → `subflowNoticeTrap`; the residue is `builtin/save-notice-node.ts:66-73` (`this run holds no record write to answer …`). **Accurate.**
- `open_questions: []` — none to answer.
- Out-of-scope finding #28897 (seat-filed): a region-nested call whose child suspends fails every run and strands the child run. Not this PR's; filed. **Escalated already.**
- Dev typecheck note: the workspace `pnpm typecheck` killed the `@objectstack/spec` test-layer `tsc` on the shared box (exit `null`); run alone it exits 0. The head's `Type Check · workspace` check-run is the verdict on that, not the dev's local run: `success` at 2026-11-02T05:21Z. **Answered.**
- Shipped flows: `examples/**` and `packages/qa/**` have no region-nested `subflow` / `map` on the head (the dev's reading; consistent with the grep of every `type === 'subflow'` / `'map'` reader in the tree, which found no shipped-flow walker to contradict it). HotCRM `campaign_enrollment` (read at hotcrm `a5982564`): a `screen` flow whose two `loop` bodies call `campaign_lead_member_enroll` and `campaign_contact_member_enroll`, both `status: 'active'` with no pausing node — it still arms; switching those children off or removing them while it is enabled is now refused. That is §7.3 working, as the seat accepted.
- Check-runs on the head: every derived gate family answered by its check-run — 53 success, 11 skipped, none failed or in progress at 2026-11-02T05:21Z.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`.** ADR-0126 §7.3: "Disabling flow B is refused while any packaged flow references B as a subflow, and the refusal names the callers — otherwise a vendor flow breaks mid-run at its subflow node with an inexplicable failure." The ADR speaks of a *reference*, not of a top-level node; the engine's own docblock for `subflowTargets` calls it the single reading of "A calls B" that both directions share. A `subflow` / `map` inside a `loop` body, a `parallel` branch or a `try_catch` slot is a reference the run follows on every pass. So on `main` the spec declared a refusal the runtime delivered only for one node position: that is Prime Directive #10's "declared ≠ enforced", and the right repair is the one taken — implement the declared refusal at every call site, bulk paths included — not to narrow the claim. The diff takes no declared capability away at the consumer: registration, the save door and `objectstack validate` accept the same flows; what moves is arming and the child's switch-off / removal, which §7.3 already reserved. **The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real.**

**The card's three wants, in the tree**: (1) measured first — the dev's 6/6 region cases armed and the top-level twins declined, consistent with the old body's `for (const node of nodes)`; (2) `subflowTargets` reuses `collectFlowGraphs` — the import is from `@objectstack/spec/automation` and the body is a two-level loop over the graphs it returns, no second walker; (3) no new gate — the diff adds no guard, no `FLOW_PAUSE_CAPABLE_NODE_TYPES` change, no `ui/**`, no hotcrm change.

**Attempts to break it.**
- *A malformed region.* `collectFlowGraphs` drops non-record members and skips a slot whose `nodes` is not an array; a region the schema refused never reaches `this.flows`. Cannot throw through the guards.
- *A region-nested call to a suspending child.* Would the asymmetry (`subflowTargets` at every depth, the notice gate top-level) let a trap through? No: the only way a region-nested call could strand a notice is by suspending the caller, and `region-suspension-refusal.ts` fails the run at the boundary instead, un-routably. The two new pins hold exactly this. The asymmetry is correct, not a gap, and the header prose on both sides says why.
- *Re-judge churn.* `transitiveSubflowCallers` now returns more callers; each is re-offered only when its own reading moved (`settled`), so a region caller that is bound and trap-free is left alone.
- *The ledger-disabled cycle exemption* now sees a cycle closed through a region call; it is read with the same `subflowTargets` on both legs, so it stays symmetric.
- *A `map` whose child is disabled, in a region with an empty collection.* It declines although no pass would call the child. §7.3 refuses on the reference, and so did the top-level reading for a `decision` branch never taken; consistent.
- *The alias key.* A region-nested `subflow` carrying the retired `config.flow` alias is refused by the strict region schema at parse (and the conversion walk reads `FLOW_REGION_SLOTS_BY_TYPE`), so the guard's canonical-key-only reading is not a hole.
- *Depth.* Past `MAX_REGION_DEPTH` the call is unread — by the parse too; not a reachable shape for a flow the parse accepted.

**Findings.**
- **Must-fix: none.**
- **Should-fix 1** — the enable door is not pinned with a region-nested call. `refuseEnableOntoDisabledSubflow` (`toggleFlow(caller, true)` onto a disabled child, `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409) reads `disabledPackagedSubflows`, so it is covered by construction, and `subflow-guard-every-door.test.ts` pins that door for a top-level call only. One `it` in `subflow-guard-region-calls.test.ts` enabling a ledger-disabled packaged caller whose `loop` body calls an `obsolete` child, asserting the envelope and that the ledger row stays off, closes the "every door" set for the region shape. Not blocking: the reading is one function.
- **Should-fix 2** — the `subflow-guards.ts` header still says "Each function here is the body of the `AutomationEngine` method of the same name, moved unedited" (slice 7 of the #25222 split). `subflowTargets` is now edited in place and its own docblock was corrected to drop "moved unedited", but the file header was not. A one-line header amendment ("`subflowTargets` has since moved on, #28846") keeps the next reader from reading `engine.ts` history for a body that lives here.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · PR #28959 · 2026-11-02T05:26Z

Head-sha: `87411da83042879ee3c0d8a72a22a73ac3f99fe0`

**维护者速读(席位终稿)**
- **改了什么**:子流程守卫(ADR-0126 §7.3)现在也看见嵌在 `loop` / `parallel` / `try_catch` 区域里的 `subflow` / `map` 调用：引用了已停用子流程的打包调用方不再上膛;子流程在被区域内调用时停用、删除被拒(409,点名调用方)。以前只看顶层节点。
- **为什么改**:#28846(p3),半张 (a);半张 (b) 经席位裁定 `6568462471` 撤回，区域内挂起子流程的问题另立 #28897。
- **风险与回滚**:低。`subflowTargets` 改读规范里唯一的区域遍历 `collectFlowGraphs`,无新门禁、无新导出、无 spec 运行逻辑改动(spec 只改注释)。`save_notice` 门仍只看顶层(区域边界本就按 #18881 拒绝挂起),两条钉子守住。回滚即 revert。
- **先看**:`packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-guards.ts` 的 `subflowTargets`。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run src/subflow-guard-region-calls.test.ts`。
- **需要你做的**:无。席位按常设授权落地，合并即关 #28846。
- **席位意见**:契约复核 PASS,可落。

### 核对六项
1. **形态**:draft → `main`;`Fixes #28846`,与认领 `6568384018`、裁定 `6568462471` 一致。文件 7 个，均在申报面内(三处 spec / notice-guard 文件只改注释，复核逐块核实)。
